atoms.a0001: Irregular periods with acne, extra facial hair, or weight gain can point to PCOS or another hormonal cause. Blood tests and an ultrasound help confirm it.
atoms.a0002: Major stress, heavy exercise, dieting or weight loss can switch off ovulation temporarily and delay or stop periods. This is common and usually reversible.
atoms.a0003: A late or missed period after sex can mean pregnancy. A home urine test is accurate from the first day of a missed period.
atoms.a0004: Tiredness, weight change, palpitations, hair loss, or irregular periods can come from an under- or over-active thyroid. A simple blood test (TSH) checks this.
atoms.a0005: Unusual discharge, odour, itching, burning or pelvic pain can come from vaginal yeast or bacterial infection, or a sexually transmitted infection. A clinician can test and treat the right cause.
atoms.a0006: Starting, stopping or changing birth-control pills, injections or an IUD often changes the pattern of bleeding, and periods can take a few months to settle or return.
atoms.a0007: Fibroids and ovarian cysts are common. They can cause heavy or painful periods or pelvic discomfort and are diagnosed with an ultrasound.
atoms.a0008: No single explanation stood out for your answers. Late or irregular periods are common and have many causes, including pregnancy, stress, thyroid or hormone changes.
atoms.a0009: Severe one-sided lower belly pain or heavy bleeding when you might be pregnant needs same-hour emergency assessment.
atoms.a0010: Soaking a pad every hour for two hours or more, or feeling faint, can lead to dangerous blood loss.
atoms.a0011: Raised itchy welts often come from an allergy or infection, and many settle within hours to days.
atoms.a0012: Thick, silvery-white scaly plaques on the elbows, knees, scalp or lower back suggest psoriasis. It is a long-term, treatable skin condition.
atoms.a0013: Dry, itchy, red, or scaly patches are often eczema or contact dermatitis. They flare with irritants and dry skin.
atoms.a0014: Intense itching that is worse at night, especially between the fingers and around the wrists or waist, with others at home affected, suggests scabies. It needs a medicated cream or lotion.
atoms.a0015: Itchy, ring-shaped, or scaly patches, often in warm folds, are usually fungal and respond to antifungal cream.
atoms.a0016: A red, itchy or blistering rash where something touched the skin, such as a soap, cream, jewellery, plant or hair dye, is likely contact dermatitis.
atoms.a0017: Tiny red bumps in sweaty or covered areas in hot weather are heat rash, and rough, flaky skin is often simple dryness. Both are harmless.
atoms.a0018: Rashes with fever or small clusters of blisters or warts can be viral, such as chickenpox, measles, or cold sores. Many clear by themselves, but some need testing or treatment.
atoms.a0019: Red, warm, painful, or pus-filled skin can be a bacterial infection that sometimes needs antibiotics.
atoms.a0020: Swelling of the lips, tongue, or throat, drooling, or noisy breathing can close the airway. This is an emergency even if you feel only mildly unwell.
atoms.a0021: Widespread blistering, peeling skin, or sores in the mouth or eyes after starting a medicine can be a serious drug reaction.
atoms.a0022: Fever with a stiff neck, severe headache, confusion, or a rash that does not fade when pressed can mean meningitis or a blood infection. Hospital treatment is needed straight away.
atoms.a0023: Severe, wave-like pain in the side or back that moves toward the groin, sometimes with blood in the urine, suggests a kidney stone and needs a scan.
atoms.a0024: Back pain that shoots down a leg, with tingling, can come from a disc pressing on a nerve. Many settle with rest, physiotherapy, and time.
atoms.a0025: Neck wear and tear can cause neck stiffness, headaches at the back of the head, and pain or tingling spreading to the shoulder or arm.
atoms.a0026: Aching that builds slowly with use and eases with rest, with brief morning stiffness, in the knees, hips, spine or finger joints over age 50, suggests osteoarthritis.
atoms.a0027: Pain, bruising, or swelling after a fall, twist, or heavy lift can be a sprain, strain, or sometimes a fracture. A doctor can decide whether an X-ray is needed.
atoms.a0028: Pain shooting from the buttock down one leg below the knee, sometimes with tingling, suggests an irritated sciatic nerve, most often from a disc. Most cases improve over weeks.
atoms.a0029: Back pain and stiffness that is worst in the early morning or at night and eases with exercise, starting before age 40, can be inflammatory back pain (spondyloarthritis). Early treatment prevents stiffening.
atoms.a0030: New numbness around the groin, loss of bladder or bowel control, or sudden leg weakness with back pain needs an urgent spinal scan. Delay can cause permanent damage.
atoms.a0031: Back pain after a serious fall, road accident, or heavy blow can mean a fracture or internal injury.
atoms.a0032: Fever with back or side pain and urinary symptoms can mean the infection has reached the kidney. It needs a urine test and antibiotics the same day.
atoms.a0033: Passing a lot of urine, constant thirst, tiredness, tingling, or slow healing can come from raised blood sugar. A blood sugar test is quick and confirms it.
atoms.a0034: A weak or slow stream, getting up at night to pass urine, or a feeling of not emptying fully, in men over 40, suggests an enlarged prostate. A doctor can examine you and arrange tests.
atoms.a0035: Burning when you pass urine, passing urine often, or lower belly discomfort suggests a urinary infection. A urine test confirms it, and antibiotics usually clear it.
atoms.a0036: No single explanation stood out for your answers. Urine problems have many causes, from infection and dehydration to stones or diabetes.
atoms.a0037: Being unable to pass any urine, especially with lower belly pain, needs a catheter or relief the same day.
atoms.a0038: High fever with shaking chills and severe back or side pain can mean a kidney infection that has reached the blood.
atoms.a0039: Burning upper belly pain that comes with hunger or meals can be gastritis or an ulcer, often linked to H. pylori bacteria or anti-inflammatory painkillers.
atoms.a0040: Pain in the upper right belly, often after fatty meals and lasting an hour or more, can be gallstones. An ultrasound confirms it.
atoms.a0041: Cramping belly pain with bloating, and changes in stool that ease after a bowel movement, over months, fit irritable bowel syndrome. It is a diagnosis made after other causes are excluded.
atoms.a0042: Pain that starts around the navel and moves to the lower right belly, especially with fever or loss of appetite, can be appendicitis and needs a same-day examination.
atoms.a0043: Sudden vomiting, loose stools, cramps, and low fever, especially after a suspect meal, are usually a stomach infection that clears in 2 to 3 days.
atoms.a0044: Burning or sour-tasting acid coming up from the stomach is common and usually settles with diet and habit changes.
atoms.a0045: Hard, infrequent stools with straining or a feeling of incomplete emptying are common and usually respond to diet and routine changes.
atoms.a0046: No single explanation stood out for your answers. Stomach pain has many causes and most are not serious, but where it hurts and how it behaves matters.
atoms.a0047: Severe constant belly pain, a hard rigid belly, or pain that keeps you from moving can mean a surgical emergency.
atoms.a0048: Vomiting blood, black tarry stools, or passing blood can mean internal bleeding that needs urgent treatment.
atoms.a0049: High fever with chills, severe body ache, headache, or rash, especially after mosquito exposure or travel, needs a blood test for malaria or dengue the same day.
atoms.a0050: Cough with fever, chest pain on breathing, or breathlessness can be a chest infection. A doctor should listen to your chest and may order an X-ray.
atoms.a0051: A fever lasting 5 days or more that rises step by step, with abdominal discomfort, constipation or loose stools, especially after eating outside food or drinking untreated water, can be typhoid. It needs a blood test and antibiotics from a doctor.
atoms.a0052: Fever with aches, tiredness, and a cold or cough is most often viral. It usually settles within 3 to 5 days without antibiotics.
atoms.a0053: A painful throat with fever and swollen tonsils can be viral or bacterial. A doctor can check whether antibiotics are needed.
atoms.a0054: A cough or fever lasting more than 2 to 3 weeks, with night sweats or weight loss, needs a chest X-ray and sputum test to rule out tuberculosis.
atoms.a0055: A cold causes a runny nose, sneezing, sore throat, and cough. It is caused by a virus, so antibiotics do not help, and it usually clears in 7 to 10 days.
atoms.a0056: Fever in a baby under 3 months, a very high temperature, fits, or confusion needs emergency assessment.
atoms.a0057: Struggling to breathe, being unable to speak a full sentence, or blue lips needs emergency treatment. It can worsen within minutes.
atoms.a0058: Fever with loose stools or stomach upset that does not clear can come from a bowel infection or parasite and may need a stool test.
atoms.a0059: Symptoms that began soon after starting or changing a medicine may be a side effect. Many common medicines cause nausea, dizziness or stomach upset.
atoms.a0060: Anxiety can cause a racing heart, tight chest, breathlessness, nausea, and tingling. It is real, common, and treatable, but other causes should be ruled out first.
atoms.a0061: A throbbing, often one-sided headache with nausea and sensitivity to light or sound fits migraine. Treatment works best when started early.
atoms.a0062: Being unable to keep any fluids down, passing almost no urine, or being very drowsy means you probably need fluids through a drip.
atoms.a0063: Wheeze, chest tightness, and a cough that is worse at night, with cold air, or after exercise suggest asthma or a sensitive airway. A breathing test confirms it.
atoms.a0064: Sneezing, a blocked or runny nose, itchy eyes, or a dry cough triggered by dust, pollen, or pets suggests allergy.
atoms.a0065: A dry, tickly cough that started after beginning a blood-pressure tablet ending in “-pril” is a well-known side effect.
atoms.a0066: A long-standing cough with phlegm and breathlessness in a smoker or someone exposed to dust or fumes can be chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. A breathing test (spirometry) confirms it.
atoms.a0067: A cough with phlegm after a cold is usually viral bronchitis. It settles by itself, often over 2 to 3 weeks, and antibiotics rarely help.
atoms.a0068: Coughing up blood needs a doctor and usually a chest X-ray the same day.
atoms.a0069: Sudden surges of intense fear that peak within minutes, with pounding heart, shaking, sweating or breathlessness, suggest panic attacks. They feel dangerous but pass, and treatment works.
atoms.a0070: Persistent worry about many things, with tension, restlessness and poor sleep for months, suggests generalized anxiety. It responds well to talking therapy, medicine, or both.
atoms.a0071: Persistent low mood, loss of interest, poor sleep, or tiredness are signs of depression. It is common and treatable with talking therapy, medicine, or both.
atoms.a0072: Coffee, tea, energy drinks, nicotine, decongestants and stimulants can cause a racing heart, shakiness, anxiety and poor sleep.
atoms.a0073: Thoughts of ending your life or hurting yourself are a medical emergency. You do not have to face them alone, and help works.
atoms.a0074: Chest pressure, pain spreading to the arm or jaw, fainting, or breathlessness with these symptoms can mean a heart or lung emergency. Do not wait for it to pass or try home remedies.
atoms.a0075: Neck pain with tingling, numbness or shooting pain down one arm can come from a pinched nerve in the neck. Most cases improve with time and physiotherapy.
atoms.a0076: Tingling or numbness in the thumb, index and middle fingers that wakes you at night, and eases when you shake the hand, suggests pressure on the median nerve at the wrist.
atoms.a0077: Numbness, tingling or burning in both feet and sometimes the hands suggests damage to the nerves of the limbs. Common causes are diabetes, low vitamin B12, alcohol and thyroid problems.
atoms.a0078: Tingling, numbness, tiredness, or aches can come from low vitamin B12 or other vitamins, especially with a vegetarian diet.
atoms.a0079: No single explanation stood out for your answers. Tingling and numbness can come from a pinched nerve, low vitamins, diabetes, or anxiety.
atoms.a0080: Sudden weakness, face drooping, slurred speech, or loss of vision can mean a stroke. Treatment works best in the first hours, so do not wait to see if it passes.
atoms.a0081: Morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes, with painful swelling in several joints, can mean inflammatory arthritis. Early treatment prevents joint damage.
atoms.a0082: Bone or muscle aches and tiredness can come from low vitamin D or calcium. A blood test checks levels.
atoms.a0083: Sudden severe pain, redness and swelling of one joint, often the big toe and often overnight, suggests gout from uric acid crystals.
atoms.a0084: Pain around a joint with particular movements, such as lifting the arm, elbow pain or heel pain, often comes from irritated tendons or bursae after overuse.
atoms.a0085: A hot, red, swollen joint with fever, especially if you cannot move it, can be an infected joint that needs urgent drainage and antibiotics.
atoms.a0086: Obvious deformity, being unable to bear weight, or severe pain after an injury needs an X-ray today.
atoms.a0087: Chest discomfort that comes with effort or stress can come from the heart. This needs an ECG and a doctor’s check soon, even if the pain has gone.
atoms.a0088: Sharp, localised pain that changes with movement, breathing, or pressing on the area is often from the muscles or ribs and is not dangerous.
atoms.a0089: No single explanation stood out for your answers. Chest pain has many causes, from muscle strain and acid reflux to heart problems, so it should be checked.
atoms.a0090: Feeling tired, pale, or breathless on effort can come from low iron or low blood count. A simple blood test confirms it.
atoms.a0091: Loud snoring with pauses in breathing, waking unrefreshed and daytime sleepiness can mean obstructive sleep apnea. A sleep study confirms it, and treatment helps.
atoms.a0092: Difficulty falling or staying asleep, or waking unrefreshed, is very common and often improves with sleep habits. It can also be a symptom of anxiety, depression or other conditions.
atoms.a0093: Short spinning spells triggered by turning in bed or tilting the head are often from the inner ear (BPPV) and respond well to simple head manoeuvres done by a clinician.
atoms.a0094: Constant severe spinning for hours to days, with nausea or vomiting and trouble walking, often after a cold or flu, suggests inflammation of the balance nerve. It needs same-day assessment to be sure it is not a stroke.
atoms.a0095: Skipped or thumping beats are often harmless extra beats, but an ECG is needed to be sure of the rhythm.
atoms.a0096: Vomiting and loose stools lose water and salts. Replacing them in small, frequent sips is the key treatment.
atoms.a0097: Feeling lightheaded when you stand up fast is often a brief drop in blood pressure from dehydration, medicine, or standing for long periods.
atoms.a0098: Shakiness, sweating, hunger, weakness and lightheadedness that ease after eating can come from low blood sugar, especially after skipped meals or with diabetes medicine.
atoms.a0099: No single explanation stood out for your answers. Dizziness has many causes, including dehydration, low blood pressure, inner ear problems, and anaemia.
atoms.a0100: Breathlessness on effort, needing extra pillows at night, and swollen ankles can come from the heart not pumping well. This needs an exam, ECG and blood tests soon.
atoms.a0101: No single explanation stood out for your answers. Breathlessness has many causes, from asthma and anxiety to heart and lung problems, so it should be checked.
atoms.a0102: Facial pressure, a blocked nose, and thick nasal mucus after a cold suggest sinusitis. Most cases are viral and settle by themselves.
atoms.a0103: Drooling, being unable to swallow saliva, a muffled voice, or noisy breathing can mean the throat is closing. This is an emergency.
atoms.a0104: Taking painkillers on more than 10 to 15 days a month can itself cause daily or near-daily headaches that return as each dose wears off.
atoms.a0105: Very severe pain around one eye, with a red watering eye or blocked nostril on that side, in short attacks at similar times each day, suggests cluster headache. It needs a doctor’s assessment because specific treatments work and ordinary painkillers usually do not.
atoms.a0106: A dull, tight, band-like pressure on both sides of the head, without nausea, is typical of tension-type headache and is the most common kind.
atoms.a0107: Tired, aching eyes and a headache after long screen time or reading often come from eye strain or a need for glasses.
atoms.a0108: High blood pressure often has no symptoms but can cause headaches or dizziness. It needs repeated readings and a doctor’s review.
atoms.a0109: A headache that reaches full strength within seconds, or the worst headache of your life, needs emergency scanning.
atoms.a0110: Headache after a head injury with vomiting, drowsiness, confusion, or a seizure needs urgent scanning.
atoms.a0111: Waves of sadness after a loss or major life change are a normal response and usually ease with time and support.
atoms.a0112: Low mood together with past episodes of unusually high energy, little need for sleep or racing thoughts may point to bipolar disorder, which is treated differently from depression alone.
atoms.a0113: Low mood that lasts for weeks deserves a conversation with a doctor or counsellor. Effective treatments exist.
atoms.a0114: Acne comes from blocked oil glands and is very common. Gentle, consistent skin care helps most cases.
atoms.a0115: Deep, painful lumps that scar are best treated early by a doctor or skin specialist, because over-the-counter products rarely control them.
atoms.a0116: Spots that began after a new cosmetic, hair oil or sunscreen, or after steroids, anabolic supplements or certain medicines, may be triggered by that product.
atoms.a0117: Persistent redness over the cheeks and nose with flushing, visible small blood vessels or pimple-like bumps, but no blackheads, can be rosacea rather than acne.
atoms.a0118: Small itchy or tender red bumps around hair follicles, often after shaving, sweating or tight clothing, are usually folliculitis.
atoms.a0119: No single explanation stood out for your answers. Acne is common and responds to gentle, consistent skin care.
